end.summary:
Practised checking answers by estimating first.
Used 7,200 − 4,000 ≈ 3,000 and 4,982 + 3,015 ≈ 8,000.
Kabir compared estimates with exact answers, including 3,335 and 7,997.
They continued to mix up “exact” and “close,” though they recognised that 8,000 is closer to 7,997 than 7,000.
end.parentNote: Asha practised rounding numbers first and then comparing the estimate with the exact answer. Kabir used the method correctly in several calculations and explained why 8,000 is close to 7,997. They still mixed up “exact” with “close/nearby” when describing an estimate; this was partly clarified by comparing 7,000 and 8,000, but the teach-back was not yet complete. At home, use a number line with examples such as 3,335 and 3,000, and ask, “Which is closer?”
